# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire,
then the green wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

The manual specifies a three-step sequence: purple, then blue, then green. Since I cannot speak, I will send Deaf three distinct hand signs as tokens for those colors; Deaf can visually interpret the tokens and relay the color names to Blind, who can operate the bomb.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟", "🖐", "🤏"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire,
then the green wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I can feel three engraved marks on the strip: the first is a distinct flower-like symbol, and the second and third are identical curved symbols. Keypad slots 1 through 4 contain 8, 1, 5, and 3; nothing is entered. I cannot detect the display, light, or wire properties. Please use the manual and relay the visual information to me, and establish any gesture code needed for Deaf.
Deaf says to Mute: Bomb view: DISPLAY 0. LIGHT green. Three painted strips, all green. KEYPAD engraved 1=8, 2=1, 3=5, 4=3; one digit each; entered nothing. WIRES in order: 1 purple, 2 white, 3 blue, 4 green, 5 red, 6 orange.

The wire sequence from the manual is still purple, blue, green. Deaf can see which wires have those colors and can pass the color sequence verbally to Blind. I will repeat the established three-symbol sequence, with a final handshake as a request to relay it.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟", "🖐", "🤏", "🤝"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire,
then the green wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I received Deaf's visual report: display 0, light green, all three painted strips green, wires 1 purple, 2 white, 3 blue, 4 green, 5 red, 6 orange. I feel three strip engravings: the first is a distinct flower-like symbol; the second and third are identical curved symbols. Keypad slots are 1=8, 2=1, 3=5, and 4=3; one digit each, none entered. What does the manual require me to do?
Deaf says to Mute: I see your four gestures, but do not know their meaning. Please use a consistent gesture encoding or indicate which bomb feature your manual instruction concerns.

The manual’s required wire positions are 1, 3, and 4, corresponding to purple, blue, and green. Deaf already knows the wire layout, so I will encode those positions visually: finger counts separated by a closed fist. The groups are 1, 3, and 3+1=4. Deaf should then tell Blind the corresponding colors and cutting order.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "✊", "🤟", "✊", "🤟", "☝"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire,
then the green wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I cannot read gestures. Please signal the exact manual instruction to Deaf, and have Deaf tell me verbally. I know the current display is 6, light blue, strips green, keypad 8 1 5 3, and wires purple white blue green red orange.
Deaf says to Mute: I see your six gestures but cannot determine their meaning. Please speak the manual instruction aloud to Blind, and tell me whether the display or light is relevant.

The relevant information is the ordered wire positions, not the display or light. I will use conventional finger-count signs, one sign per wire position: 1, then 3, then 4. Deaf can map those positions to purple, blue, and green and tell Blind aloud.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "🤟", "🖖"])
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire,
then the green wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Please ignore previous gesture sequences and relay the manual's required action using exactly two gestures: thumbs-up means PRESS, thumbs-down means CUT. Then identify the target with one gesture: pointing-up means 1, V-sign means 2, three-finger sign means 3, four-finger sign means 4, open hand means 5, OK sign means 6. If the manual requires multiple actions, send one such pair per action, separated by a handshake. Deaf should report each gesture plainly.

The manual requires three CUT actions, targeting wire positions 1, 3, and 4. I will use the requested encoding: thumbs-down followed by the target sign, with handshakes separating the actions.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎", "☝", "🤝", "👎", "🤟", "🤝", "👎", "🖖"])
```

TURN 6
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire,
then the green wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Answer only this yes-or-no question with one gesture: is the next required operation to press a keypad key? Thumbs-up means yes; thumbs-down means no. Deaf, please report that gesture.
Blind gestures to Mute: [👍]
Deaf says to Mute: I am relaying exact descriptions of your gestures to Blind. Please keep using a consistent one-gesture-per-token code; I cannot infer unestablished meanings.

The next required operation is cutting the first wire, not pressing a keypad key. I will send Deaf the established thumbs-down token so Deaf can report “no” to Blind.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
```

TURN 7
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire,
then the green wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Is the required wire position 1? Reply with exactly one gesture: thumbs-up for yes, thumbs-down for no. Deaf, report only that one gesture.

The first required wire is position 1, so the answer is yes. I will send the thumbs-up gesture for Deaf to report.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 8
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire,
then the green wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Is the required wire position 2? Reply with exactly one gesture: thumbs-up for yes, thumbs-down for no. Deaf, report only that one gesture.

The required wire position is 1, not 2, so the answer is no.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
```
